results.output: Harbor-wide barrier systems generally exhibit low cost-effectiveness and low benefit-cost ratios (BCRs)—typically ranging from 0.05 to 0.33 at a 7% discount rate and 0.20 to 1.69 at a 3% discount rate when shore-based systems function as designed—whereas shore-based solutions have the potential for high cost-effectiveness [1]. While barrier BCRs can increase (such as to 3.69–5.42 if shore-based measures are ineffective and a 3% discount rate is used), most BCRs remain under 1.0 when shore-site adaptation is effective [1]. Regarding funding, these low benefit-cost ratios for harbor-wide barriers make eligibility for federal funding very challenging, if not impossible [1].
